title: Reported Speech: Tense and Universal Truths — Quiz 124
content:
## Reported Speech: Tense and Universal Truths

Choose the reported tense and notice when a general truth stays unchanged.

### Lesson focus

1. They said, “Honesty is the best policy.”
2. My neighbour says, “Good days will come.”
3. My neighbour said, “Good days will come.”

### Understand the pattern

Backshift is not a rule that every past report must always follow. Proverbs and statements the reporter treats as still valid often keep their tense. A present reporting verb normally leaves the original tense unchanged.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. They said that honesty is the best policy.
2. My neighbour says that good days will come.
3. My neighbour said that good days would come.

In the third answer, would marks the future as seen from the earlier moment of speaking; it need not describe a present promise.

### Try another

Report as an enduring statement: The teacher said, 'The Earth orbits the Sun.'

### Suggested answer

The teacher said that the Earth orbits the Sun. Keeping present simple presents the fact as continuing to hold.
